correctness.rationale: All primitive constant-action period-two orbits require sin(2πx_0)=sin(2πx_1)=0 and therefore alternate angles 0 and 1/2; the congruence W(y)=m+1/2 is necessary and sufficient. The even quartic has only one minimum as a function of y squared, giving central roots and an exact closed-cutoff staircase with strict lower endpoint. Direct multiplication of the two exact unit-determinant Jacobians yields trace 2-(2πbW prime)^2. Strict convexity on the positive outer branch makes its unique stability threshold; asymptotic inversion of W gives the stated m^(3/2) spectral radius. The packaged verify.py passed 945 assertions, including exact rational Jacobian and endpoint/root checks. These checks do not substitute for the infinite analytic proof.

originality.rationale: Direct comparisons of the complete 2023 source paper, 2023 full preprint and 2024 accessible full manuscript show symmetry-axis and local periodic-orbit ingredients but no all-integer, all-action half-turn two-cycle census, exact R-dependent quartic staircase, or sharp universal Floquet tail. Targeted published mathematical-record searches returned nearest classifications for different maps only. Differences are in hypotheses and mathematical implication, not merely naming. A stronger general reversible-map theorem could conceivably cover the elementary derivation and remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: A broader generic reversible-map or area-preserving kick-shear theorem in unindexed literature might subsume the elementary constant-action mechanism or portions of the staircase; targeted checks did not locate a decisive covering result.
Large action in the exact mathematical map is outside the physical approximation region discussed in the source model; this limits physical significance, not the theorem.

value.rationale: For a physically motivated nontwist plasma-transport map, the zero-action-transport primitive two-cycles are a canonical symmetry-constrained class. This result exhausts that natural class globally at every angular winding (not arbitrary two-cycles), supplies an exact quartic action-cutoff resonance staircase and shows an elliptic-to-hyperbolic boundary with infinitely many increasingly hyperbolic surviving orbits for every b>0. These are structurally motivated invariant counts and stability facts distinct from the literature’s local resonance/transport plots, not arbitrary finite computations; large-action physical limits and lack of nonlinear stability claims are explicit.
